evidence.note: 本轮独立定义审计（未修改题卡、无数学程序执行）：{"correct_statement":"For every compact convex polygon P in R^2 with nonempty interior and every integer n>=1, there exist compact convex sets P_1,...,P_n with nonempty interior such that union_i P_i=P, int(P_i) intersect int(P_j) is empty for i!=j, area(P_i)=area(P)/n for all i, and perim(P_i)=perim(P_j) for all i,j.","equivalent_perimeter_form":"There exists a common real number p>0 such that perim(P_i)=p for all i. The common p is not required to equal perim(P)/n; for a nontrivial partition it is strictly larger than that number.","boundary_checks":["n must be a positive integer. If a convention includes zero in N, the bare expression n in N is insufficient: division by zero and an empty union do not describe a partition of a positive-area polygon.","n=1 is trivial: P_1=P. Both the correct condition and the card's incorrect formula happen to agree only at this boundary.","A convex body means compact, convex and with nonempty interior, as the actual theorem explicitly states. Degenerate segments, points or the empty set are outside this domain.","Positive area of P together with equal area area(P)/n ensures each piece has positive area; for a planar convex compact set this implies nonempty interior.","The pieces need only have disjoint interiors. Their closed boundaries may overlap along cut interfaces. Requiring closed pieces themselves to be pairwise disjoint would exclude ordinary subdivisions.","Perimeter is the full Euclidean length of the boundary of each piece, including new internal cut edges. It is not just the portion inherited from the boundary of P.","The explicit interiors-disjoint convention should be kept for clarity. In a finite convex covering with each area exactly area(P)/n, the equality of total areas already rules out positive-area overlaps, so the omission of that clause alone is not the decisive error in the card."]}

evidence.note: 此证据仅独立核原定理到建议修正目标的适用性，不把同一论文重复当多份独立全证明。{"exact_scope_in_paraphrase":"Every convex body K in the plane has a partition into m convex parts with equal areas and equal perimeters, for every integer m>=2.","interface_checks":["Every compact positive-area convex polygon is a convex compactum with nonempty interior and hence is directly an allowed K; no approximation of the polygon by smooth bodies is needed for this implication.","Ordinary Euclidean perimeter is a continuous scalar functional on planar convex bodies in the Hausdorff metric, and is explicitly the motivating functional in the theorem. Ordinary area is included in the theorem's allowed absolutely continuous measures.","The equality requirement is equality of all function values. Page 2 makes this explicit by quotienting the vector of piece perimeters by the diagonal {(t,...,t)}. There is no equation prescribing that diagonal value as perim(K)/m.","All integers m>=2 are covered in this v14 theorem, not only primes, prime powers, or twice prime powers. Page 2 explicitly distinguishes the general Sections 4-5 argument from the separate twice-prime-power discussion in Section 3.","Adding the trivial n=1 case gives the corrected statement for every positive integer n.","The paper defines its convex bodies to have nonempty interior and says its proof never applies the functional to a body with empty interior. Ordinary positive area also prevents zero-area final pieces."],"existence_versus_construction":"Page 1 says the proof builds a solution recursively and explains that its validity is established by induction and a separation lemma. The theorem itself is an existence statement. It does not, merely by that wording, promise a specified exact-coordinate algorithm, complexity bound, numerical error certificate, or finite symbolic output for arbitrary real input polygons. The card's extra demand to give a construction method should either mean the mathematical proof's construction or be separated into a precisely specified additional algorithmic task; it must not silently replace the original existence question.","verification_depth":"Actual primary theorem and scope read, followed by independent elementary application to the card. No independent verification of all topology, configuration-space or separation-lemma details is claimed here. The academic and root reviews of Sections 4-5 and publication/version history are recorded separately; they do not expand this auditor's own reading scope.","conclusion":"The corrected original existence question is directly the theorem's scope. The literal perim(P)/n statement remains false and must be amended before assigning the original theorem to a repaired card revision."}
